look_here_first: Look at the samara first: green ash has a larger seed body with the wing decurrent well down the body before broadening; then confirm a broad shield-shaped leaf scar and usually non-glaucous lower leaflet surface.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: opposite branches and odd-pinnate leaves, usually 5–7(9) leaflets

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: broad shield-shaped to oblong-ovate leaf scar

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: samara body >1.5 cm with wing extending well down the seed body

key_traits.label: Leaf morphology
key_traits.text: Usually 5–7(9) leaflets; margins subentire to inconspicuously dentate-serrulate.

key_traits.label: Abaxial surface
key_traits.text: Generally glabrous/non-glaucous compared with Texas ash.

key_traits.label: Leaf scar
key_traits.text: Shield-shaped to broadly oblong-ovate; upper edge truncate to shallowly concave.

key_traits.label: Fruit
key_traits.text: Consistently 2-winged samara in the Central Texas comparison; wing runs down proximal body then broadens distally.
